correctness.rationale: The connected-graph correspondence with unlabeled rooted forests is established by universal-root decomposition. The exact integer recurrence D(T)=z(1+z)^(n-1)+product_i D(T_i), singleton D=z, counts dominating subsets, including omission of the root. Independently implemented canonical multiset enumeration, unrelated to saved verifier output, generated all rooted-tree shapes at n=1..16 with counts 1,1,2,4,9,20,48,115,286,719,1842,4766,12486,32973,87811,235381 (376464 total). Every n<=15 shape passed all local log-concavity inequalities; at n=16 exactly the root with three chain-length-five child subtrees failed. Exact witness coefficients (0,1,15,230,1205,3615,7378,11080,12735,11410,8005,4368,1820,560,120,16,1) satisfy 15^2<230. For disconnected graphs, domination polynomials multiply, and convolution of nonnegative log-concave sequences without internal zeros is log-concave; a disconnected 16-vertex graph has strictly smaller components. The independent search explicitly verified the whole finite class; no assertion about least obstruction within larger n than required.

value.rationale: The ordinary domination polynomial is a natural counting invariant; log-concavity is a structural coefficient property important for its shape. The theorem locates the first failure and certifies uniqueness in the hereditary trivially-perfect class, with a transparent graph witness and exact 16-vertex extremal boundary. This is materially more than reporting a known windmill polynomial or a sampled counterexample.
